# Pinned Blender for the content build. tools/bake.sh verifies the hash before use.
#
# Pinned to an exact binary rather than a version range because bpy is a stateful
# tool whose defaults and operators shift between releases; version pinning is what
# buys back determinism. The bpy pip wheel is a documented fallback, but the binary
# is preferred: the wheel hard-couples Blender's minor version to a specific CPython,
# which makes agent sandboxes fragile.
#
# Verified working 2026-08-09: headless geometry, custom float attributes, smart UV
# project, Cycles CPU AO bake, GLB export — all green in ~0.8 s for a test mesh.

BLENDER_VERSION=4.5.3
BLENDER_URL=https://download.blender.org/release/Blender4.5/blender-4.5.3-linux-x64.tar.xz
BLENDER_SHA256=975c58fcb244273838534bba771e64ad87739216b0f9b39a888531a49a72d845
BLENDER_DIR=blender-4.5.3-linux-x64

# Fallback, if the binary cannot run in a given environment:
#   pip install bpy==4.5.*        # requires Python 3.11

cd /home/runner/work/polecat-platform/polecat-platform/chicago/chicago/4d && cat > docs/RESEARCH/second-fort-cupola-T-2388/README.md <<'EOF'
# The second fort's blockhouse cupola — before and after (T-2388, partial)

Two renders of the same 21-member compound, from **one identical camera**, with nothing changed
between them but the blockhouse's own bytes:

| | master | sha256 |
|---|---|---|
| `before/` | `fort_dearborn_blockhouse__log_1816.glb` | `4b49f0dba271d11ce407e6b407c6e4a766402bce04b93b24ebbcc2862f899e00` |
| `after/` | `fort_dearborn_blockhouse__log_1816.glb` | `96d9fb803cdd3b1639c32b9e0c562d0b3bf2af1b2fe8254abea4d62e8e136b15` |

The picture on the left of each pair is `data/sources/assets/prefire_views_kevin_2026_08/p3_1.png`
(sha256 `80c71433…`), panel 5 of the Kurz & Allison sheet of 1893, captioned "Fort Dearborn as
rebuilt 1835". **Before**: a brick stack standing at the apex of the blockhouse's cap, invented
and unattested, where the panel draws a cupola. **After**: the small square cupola under its own
four-sided cap, seated into all four roof planes, and no stack.

## What this camera is, and is not

`second-fort-panel-5-compound.json` copies every number of the T-3040 landmark fit
(`docs/RESEARCH/fort-reference-groups-T-3040/second-fort-panel-5.json`, preserved untouched) so
that the before and after differ by the geometry alone. That fit reached its imposed **100 m eye
bound**, both stockade endpoints are cropped, and the drawing compresses the compound, so the
whole fort renders aerial and undersized against a nearly level printed view. It is marked
`diagnostic_only`, which is the picture compiler's instruction not to offer its pose as a
historical "from this spot". **It is a control for one change, not a solved historical camera**,
and nothing in the model was moved to fit it.

## What is settled here and what is not

`second-fort-panel-5-compound.match.json` carries the verdict, which is **`differs`**. Exactly
one difference is marked `fixed` — the roof assembly this parcel built. The camera's own fit, the
galleried range's identity, the facade openings, the other roof forms and chimney counts, and the
compound's composition all remain `open`, and the other dated pictures T-2388 lists have not been
read against the model at all. The original ticket stays OPEN.

The cupola's **occurrence** is what the pictures carry. Its size, height, cap pitch and plain
boarded sides are reconstructed: see `docs/LIBERTIES.md`
§ L-second-fort-blockhouse-cupola-2388.
EOF
cd /home/runner/work/polecat-platform/polecat-platform/chicago && git add -A && git -c user.name=polecat-steward -c user.email=steward@polecat.live commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
T-2388: the second fort's blockhouse gets the cupola its pictures draw

Panel 5 of the Kurz & Allison sheet — "Fort Dearborn as rebuilt 1835" — draws a
small square cupola at the centre of this blockhouse's four-sided cap, under a
little cap of its own, and draws no stack anywhere on that roof. The two Wau-Bun
reproductions of the 1831 view draw the same body. Build it, and record the
invented, unattested centre chimney that stood in exactly its place at a count
of 0.

That count is a choice about what to DEPICT and the record says so: it is not a
finding that the blockhouse was unheated, that it had no flue, or that nothing
else stood on that roof. Pictorial silence at tier 5 is not testimony, and the
1856 Kellogg/Blanchard print (filed misleadingly as
chicago_fort_dearborn_river_mouth_1830.jpg) depicts about 1836-1849 and does
show a louvred cap and an ambiguous projection beside it — left unresolved, not
backdated.

The control is a keyword-only, default-off `cupola` on fort_structure, consumed
by a local `_cupola` helper. It is NOT the lighthouse's `lantern` (only _tower
reads that, so setting it here would add nothing), it does not route this
building through the tower builder, and it changes no shared geometry. Validation
accepts only the combination that is built — a blockhouse, a pyramid cap, no
separately generated centre stack — and bounds every dimension. The body is sunk
0.12 m below the lowest the main roof reaches under its own footprint, so it
meets all four sloping planes instead of balancing on the apex: no floating
corner, no strip of sky, nowhere to hide a stack.

Occurrence is inferred from the identified pictures; every dimension is
reconstructed in the archetype and admitted in docs/LIBERTIES.md
L-second-fort-blockhouse-cupola-2388. Everything below the roof is untouched —
surveyed seat and 8 degree rotation, the inferred 14.52 x 9.80 m footprint and
its ambiguity, 5.2 m walls, two storeys, 0.45 m jetty, loopholes, doors, palettes.

Changing the producer staled the family, so all 25 current fort_structure
MASTERs — the accepted 1832 lighthouse and the Lake House shell included — were
genuinely rebuilt on the pinned Ubuntu 26.04 / Blender 4.5.3 in two bounded
native batches. All 25 input hashes in assets/manifest.json are the regenerated
ones; exactly one master's bytes moved (134,632 -> 133,092) and its WEB
derivative was re-encoded, while the other 24 came back byte-identical and keep
their bound derivatives. No foreign registry row touched.

The picture is now on the building's card: the record cites kurz_allison_1893,
and data/structure_grades.json carries an explicit pictured ruling saying why
panel 5 is a reasonable whole picture of this named building — so the sidecar
grade derives `attested` from the rule rather than from a camera fit or a typed
value.

Before and after were captured through photo_match.mjs from one identical
camera with only the blockhouse's bytes changed, in
docs/RESEARCH/second-fort-cupola-T-2388/. The T-3040 bodies are preserved
untouched and the new camera is diagnostic_only. Only the roof assembly is
marked fixed; the view's verdict stays `differs` and T-2388 stays OPEN on the
camera's own fit, the ranges and galleries, the facade openings, the other roof
forms and chimney counts, the compound's composition and every other dated
picture it lists.

Gate: tools/check.sh --part 1/4 through 4/4, all four PASS.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
